title: Credit Suisse with Hub Dot: female networking
description: Here's a snapshot from the inspiring female networking event we hosted in partnership with Hub Dot. During the event, bankers shared thought provoking stories of how they manage their work-life balance. Credit Suisse continues to support and guide women on their career journeys through dedicated mentorship and committed leaders. Let us be part of your story!  For more information about current open positions and about working with us visit: https://www.credit-suisse.com/careers. You can also follow us on: Facebook - https://www.facebook.com/creditsuisse/  LinkedIn - https://www.linkedin.com/company/credit-suisse.

asr.full_text: Music So Hub.NET started with this little idea that I had and I was doing my music, I was raising my children I was doing my work and then Hub.NET grew and I always say I was a very accidental entrepreneur because I wasn't really planning for Hub.NET to become anything But what happened extraordinary is that there were a lot of people around me who really believed in this crazy little idea that I had. And I called them my angels, my advocates. And I think, you know, women supporting women is an extraordinrry thing. When you come across and this room is full of them, of champions, women that really want to help you and really want to support you, is the most magical experience. Everybody's told really inspiring stories and it's given me the impression that Credit Suisse has got a really open, diverse culture, where everybody's really welcoming and has different stories and backgrounds. Probably I found out when I was a little bit younger than you – I started in banking in 1980. If I had come to an event like this there would have been two of us, and there wouldn't have been an event like this, and back then I would never imagine to see a room like this and also to think that after 16 years out of the business where I left two set up a few businesses, opened a couple bars, have three children, do an art degree that I could come back into this world. I never imagined around banking would be so innovative and so creative. I feel the environment is very female supportive and very open minded, very diversified. I think investing in young talents. Women like you, it's key for such a big firm like Credit Suisse. So the advice I would like to give to you is if you really wanna know what is there for you, hear looking for success listen to stories from many different people. You will ultimately choose what is right for you and what is right for yourself. One of the things that jumped out at me was when a lady spoke about how she was told to choose between things that were not considered and she was given options for the areas she could go into and she decided to follow her own instincts, and she followed what she was passionate about, and as a result has had a really good career and a promising career. You never know who you're gonna meet, and what connections you might make and what they might inspire you to do and an event like this is a perfect place to start. Coming from a non-financial background, I'm an engineer, and it's very nice to talk to people who are open about sharing their story and telling you how they do everything that they do in their daily life. And it was pretty nice to know that no matter what your story is, if you have a passion that you want to follow, you can do it. Here I stand today two years into creditorships and having realised that in this privileged situation you can really help each other and help others.

The event setting and speech indicate employer branding and networking rather than a financial offer or a request for payment, credentials, or investment participation. Although current job openings and related social channels are promoted, the available video evidence does not connect that recruitment reference to deceptive claims or a harmful transaction.
